title: Fraud review lookup with OR across two columns of one table
prompt: Fraud review screen: about 20 calls per second, about 800 ms each. It lists the accounts that use the suspect's email
address or were referred by the suspect. Plan: Clustered Index Scan of PK_Customers (2.0M rows, about 31,000 logical
reads) with the OR as a residual filter. IX_Customers_Email exists; there is no index on ReferredByCustomerID. The
result has no key column: two household accounts with the same Email, LastName and Tier are two rows, and the
reviewers count them. Both parameters are always supplied: the API rejects NULL.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).

correct_families.description: Two seekable branches with UNION ALL. The second branch excludes the rows the first branch returned, and keeps the referred customers whose Email is NULL.
Combine the two branches on CustomerID, which removes exactly the rows that satisfy both, then fetch the output columns.
reference_sql: WHERE c.CustomerID IN (SELECT e.CustomerID FROM qe.Customers e WHERE e.Email = @Email
SELECT r.CustomerID FROM qe.Customers r WHERE r.ReferredByCustomerID = @ReferrerID);

traps.why: An account that uses the email and was also referred by the suspect satisfies both branches. UNION ALL returns it twice.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case self_referral: the suspect's own account uses the email and refers itself.

traps.why: c.Email <> @Email is not true for a NULL Email, so referred customers with no email address vanish from the second branch.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer referred by the suspect whose Email is NULL (9% of customers).

traps.why: UNION removes duplicates over Email, LastName and Tier. Two household accounts with the same values become one row.
traps.told_apart_by: Two accounts of one household with the same Email, LastName and Tier.

min_improvement.basis: The scan reads about 31,000 pages. Two seeks with a few lookups read well under 600.

key.reference_notes: With an index on each column the optimizer can answer the unchanged OR with two seeks and a union on the key. A rewrite is an alternative, not a requirement.
